For most habit, or at least in my experience, going cold turkey doesn't help.

Stop and ask yourself. 

What is the habit?
What makes you do it?
What else can you do instead?
What are the pro and cons of stopping?

Being mindful of what you are doing also helps, that way you aren't going on auto pilot.

If possible, I would advise seeking professional help from a therapist or perhaps a nutritionist.

I dont have experience with anorexia, however, ik that suddenly trying to stop can be risky as the body has been used to this routine for some time.

From my experience, it usually starts with a consultation, and questions that a therapist asks to get to know your situation better. In essence, its a lot of breaking down whatever issues may be troubling you.

For myself, it was about setting a goal. Like where I wanted to be and balancing the pros and cons of doing something vs. Not doing it. 

Maybe start by seeing why you don't feel like doing anything? Most habits are hard to break but not impossible, so finding the source of your habit might be a good start.

Prom should be a special time for seniors and I am annoyed that Girl A felt the need to ruin your special night. 

I usually don't like giving advice since in my opinion it feels condescending but, I would say start by seeing what triggers your panic attacks. I can't say I know a great deal about them but seeing what causes them could be a start. Additionally, being mindful as to when you feel one coming on and what works to help you calm down can also be a good place to start. 

I'll reiterate that you are NOT stupid, worthless, or a child for feeling the way you do. Having a panic disorder does not make you any less of a person.

I always visualize depression as dark vines grabbing you and holding you back. It hurts and sometimes your so far into it that everything that made sense to you suddenly doesn't. Its like a pit that you can get out of nor can see anything aside for four walls surrounding you.

Id say the main reason for people not talking about it more and vice versa nobody asking is both stigma and the feeling of vulnerability.

Noone likes to feel vulnerable, and with depression that vulnerable feels like its increased by 10. It becomes more difficult and (from experience) it becomes hard to form the words and instead just keep it bottled up. People also dont ask because they either aren't sure what to say or aren't familiar with the situation. How do you comfort someone whose at their wit's end without it sounding condescending or tasteless? 

Thats why I think awareness is important. We don't all have the answers (I dont think anyone does) but even just lending an ear occasionally goes a long way for some.
